qt: to the Commission Bert-Jan Ruissen (ECR), Anja Haga (PPE), Michaela Šojdrová (PPE), Ladislav Ilčić (ECR), Miriam Lexmann (PPE), Tomáš Zdechovský (PPE), Cristian Terheş (ECR) Subject:

On 17 January 2024, the non-governmental organisation Open Doors published its World Watch List 20241, which ranks the 50 countries where Christians face the most extreme persecution and discrimination because of their faith. According to the report, Christians worldwide are increasingly experiencing physical violence as well as pressure in various spheres of life. In particular, religiously motivated violence is intensifying in sub-Saharan Africa, while the number of attacks on Christian churches, shops and homes has grown enormously across regions compared to previous years. 1.
How does the Commission intend to use the findings of the World Watch List 2024?
Does the Commission agree that more attention to issues linked to freedom of religion or belief is needed in the EU’s human rights policy and the EU’s bilateral relations with third countries?
In this context, does the Commission consider the resources and capacity allocated to the EU Special Envoy for the promotion of freedom of religion or belief outside the EU to be sufficient?
at: (English version) to the Commission Bert-Jan Ruissen (ECR), Anja Haga (PPE), Michaela Šojdrová (PPE), Ladislav Ilčić (ECR), Miriam Lexmann (PPE), Tomáš Zdechovský (PPE), Cristian Terheş (ECR) (30 January 2024) Subject: Increasing persecution of Christians worldwide On 17 January 2024, the non-governmental organisation Open Doors published its World Watch List 2024 (1), which ranks the 50 countries where Christians face the most extreme persecution and discrimination because of their faith. According to the report, Christians worldwide are increasingly experiencing physical violence as well as pressure in various spheres of life. In particular, religiously motivated violence is intensifying in sub-Saharan Africa, while the number of attacks on Christian churches, shops and homes has grown enormously across regions compared to previous years. 1.
How does the Commission intend to use the findings of the World Watch List 2024?

2. Does the Commission agree that more attention to issues linked to freedom of religion or belief is needed in the EU’s human rights policy and the EU’s bilateral relations with third countries? 3. In this context, does the Commission consider the resources and capacity allocated to the EU Special Envoy for the promotion of freedom of religion or belief outside the EU to be sufficient? (8 March 2024) The Commission is regularly consulting with non-governmental organisations and taking into account the reports produced by them for the development and implementation of EU policies, as it is the case of the EU human rights policy. Freedom of religion or belief remains an essential priority of the EU’s external human rights policy. The Commission and the High Representative address violations of this right in EU relations with third countries. For instance, the EU raised its concerns regarding violations of freedom of religion or belief in more than 20 human rights dialogues with third countries over 2023. The Commission also published a global call for proposals in October 2023 to fund civil society projects related to freedom of religion or belief in third countries. As the Commission pointed out in its reply to Written Question E-002093/2023, the Special Envoy for the promotion of freedom of religion or belief outside the EU ‘can rely on the full support of the Commission services and the External Action Service’.
